reviewUnits.rationale: Adapter MINE_BLOCK reaches native destroyBlock through the FakePlayer; start/stop/abort are the native lifecycle of one semantic primitive, not three primitives.
reviewUnits.title: Block destruction

reviewUnits.rationale: Adapter USE_ITEM_ON_BLOCK is this packet's native path; it covers placement and block activation but not menu-only interactions.
reviewUnits.title: Use item on block / block activation

reviewUnits.rationale: The current Adapter exposes only USE_ITEM_ON_BLOCK; right-click-in-air item use is a distinct native operation and is not represented.
reviewUnits.reason: Whether air/hand item use is a generic primitive or content-only is unresolved.
reviewUnits.title: Use item in air / hand use

reviewUnits.blocker: Requires Round 1/2 scope decision and a product decision on attack primitives.
reviewUnits.rationale: Attack is a generic embodied operation but the Adapter has no attack command. It is recorded as a concrete gap candidate rather than silently mapped to interact.
reviewUnits.reason: Whether entity attack belongs in the public Adapter scope is unresolved.
reviewUnits.title: Entity attack

reviewUnits.blocker: Requires Round 1/2 scope decision and content-boundary review.
reviewUnits.rationale: Right-click entity interaction, including name-tag/mount/villager content, is not represented by the four current Adapter commands.
reviewUnits.reason: Whether entity interaction is a generic primitive or content-specific is unresolved.
reviewUnits.title: Entity interaction

reviewUnits.rationale: This packet changes the arm-swing state/feedback; it is not a world operation and has no Adapter command.
reviewUnits.title: Arm swing / punch animation input

reviewUnits.rationale: The robot inventory tracks a selected slot for MINE/USE, but there is no public Adapter operation to change it, so the packet itself is not mapped.
reviewUnits.reason: Whether slot selection is a public primitive or an implementation detail is unresolved.
reviewUnits.title: Selected hotbar slot

reviewUnits.rationale: The Adapter owns a 9-slot robot inventory, not a player menu. GUI container support is a documented limitation, so these packets are deliberately out of scope.
reviewUnits.title: Inventory menu operations

reviewUnits.rationale: Adapter TIMED_FLIGHT/STOP establish a velocity setpoint; these packets describe the ordinary player movement/input surface, not additional public commands.
reviewUnits.title: Player movement, orientation and input state

reviewUnits.rationale: Sign text is a concrete block-entity operation, not a generic primitive.
reviewUnits.title: Sign editing

reviewUnits.rationale: Book content editing is item-specific content, not a generic robot primitive.
reviewUnits.title: Book editing

reviewUnits.rationale: These are menu-content operations; the Adapter has no GUI-container primitive.
reviewUnits.title: Rename, trade selection and recipe placement

reviewUnits.rationale: Commands are a management surface, not ordinary embodied behavior; the Adapter must not become a command proxy.
reviewUnits.title: Commands and suggestions

reviewUnits.rationale: Chat is a player/social capability, not a world primitive.
reviewUnits.title: Chat and chat session state

reviewUnits.rationale: These change server/session settings rather than embodied robot behavior.
reviewUnits.title: Admin and session state changes

reviewUnits.rationale: Raw tag queries are operator diagnostics, not the robot's typed observation interface.
reviewUnits.title: NBT/debug tag queries

reviewUnits.rationale: These are connection/transport mechanisms. Client information is configuration, not a world operation.
reviewUnits.title: Common connection protocol

reviewUnits.rationale: These are concrete block/editor implementations dispatched through the generic use-on-block path, not primitive operations.
reviewUnits.title: Command/jigsaw/structure/test/beacon block editors

reviewUnits.rationale: Available to an ordinary client, but the previous blanket exclusion from the robot observation contract is withdrawn pending Round 3 review.
reviewUnits.reason: Clientbound observation semantics have not been reviewed; the prior EXCLUDED decision is withdrawn.
reviewUnits.title: Clientbound block observations

reviewUnits.rationale: The prior blanket exclusion is withdrawn; clientbound entity streams may carry robot-relevant self/entity state.
reviewUnits.reason: Entity observation semantics and self-state relevance are unreviewed.
reviewUnits.title: Clientbound entity observations

reviewUnits.rationale: The robot inventory is server-authoritative, but the prior clientbound exclusion is withdrawn pending the Round 3 review.
reviewUnits.reason: Whether clientbound inventory state is needed for robot self-state is unreviewed.
reviewUnits.title: Clientbound inventory observations

reviewUnits.rationale: The prior blanket exclusion is withdrawn; the observation review must decide whether client-side world state is usable evidence.
reviewUnits.reason: Clientbound world/chunk observation value is unreviewed.
reviewUnits.title: Clientbound world/chunk observations

reviewUnits.rationale: The previous CONTENT decision is provisional; Round 3 must decide whether presentation packets are outside observation or supporting feedback.
reviewUnits.reason: Presentation-vs-observation boundary is unreviewed.
reviewUnits.title: Presentation and UI feedback

reviewUnits.rationale: The robot body relies on native movement/collision; this is the embodied substrate of flight, not a separate command.
reviewUnits.title: Passive motion, collision and inside-block scanning

reviewUnits.rationale: Pressure plates, tripwire and other blocks are concrete content implementations; the generic dispatch is represented by the block state hook, not one primitive per block.
reviewUnits.title: Block-driven entity effects

reviewUnits.rationale: Swarmie does not collect drops; mining drops stay in the world. There is no pickup primitive.
reviewUnits.reason: Whether pickup belongs in the robot platform is a product decision, not a mechanical fact.
reviewUnits.title: Item pickup

reviewUnits.rationale: The robot is deliberately not a LivingEntity; damage/health is not part of the current model.
reviewUnits.title: Damage to the embodied entity

reviewUnits.rationale: Dimension changes are observed as lifecycle events, but there is no portal primitive in the Adapter.
reviewUnits.title: Portal transition

reviewUnits.rationale: Payload types are transport declarations. The API exposes registration but not a global enumeration of declared types.
reviewUnits.title: Fabric custom payload type declaration

reviewUnits.rationale: Receiver registration is a transport mechanism, not a world primitive. It is content-extensible and cannot be fully enumerated offline.
reviewUnits.title: Fabric server payload receivers

reviewUnits.blocker: Requires a product/scope decision after Round 2; no transfer command exists today.
reviewUnits.rationale: The Adapter has no transfer primitive. ItemStorage is a generic capability shape; concrete storages are content and require a live world probe.
reviewUnits.reason: Whether a generic transfer primitive is required is unresolved.
reviewUnits.title: Fabric item storage lookup and transfer

reviewUnits.rationale: These are delivery/connection mechanisms, not observations or world operations.
reviewUnits.title: Clientbound batching/configuration protocol
